column1: # Requirements of draft-fossil-delta-format-00, one normative requirement per row,
# written from the draft text. There are no delta errata.

column3: A delta is a header, zero or more segments and a trailer, concatenated with nothing between them (delta = header *segment trailer); a decoder accepts every such delta whose bounds hold.
Applying a delta a producer emitted for a source and target to that source yields the target exactly.
column4: Section 5 states this informatively; every producer requirement presupposes it, so the cases check it as the producer's baseline.

column3: A producer writes every integer in canonical form: base 64, most significant digit first, no leading zeros, and zero as the single digit 0.
Digits 0-9 have values 0-9, A-Z 10-35, _ 36, a-z 37-62 and ~ 63, and a multi-digit integer is read most significant digit first.
Reading an integer stops at the first byte that is not a digit; that byte is the opcode or separator that follows the integer.
A decoder that accepts an integer field with no digits treats it as zero; it may reject such a delta instead.
A decoder that accepts an integer field with leading zeros uses its decoded value; it may reject such a delta instead.
A producer emits only integer values below 2^32.
column4: Create refuses a source or target of 2^32 bytes or more with ErrTooLarge (#279); unit test TestCheckSizes in internal/delta covers the bound on lengths. No conformance case: a direct one needs a 4 GiB input.

column3: A decoder rejects a delta whose header integer is not immediately followed by 0x0a.
A copy segment (count @ offset ,) appends count bytes of the source starting at zero-based byte position offset.
A decoder rejects a copy segment whose offset is not followed by a comma (0x2c).
A copy segment with count zero copies zero bytes, not the rest of the source (Appendix A).
A producer never emits a copy segment with count zero.
A literal segment (count : payload) appends the count bytes that follow the colon.
A reader consumes exactly count payload bytes without scanning them for a separator; any byte in a payload, 0x0a included, is data.
A producer always ends a delta with a trailer (checksum ;) carrying the checksum of the target, including when the target is empty.
The checksum is the sum modulo 2^32 of the target's big-endian 32-bit words, plus any 1 to 3 trailing bytes added as z[0]<<24, z[1]<<16 and z[2]<<8.
A decoder that verifies the checksum rejects a delta whose trailer does not match the reconstructed target.
column4: go-libfossil always verifies; the non-verifying branch of the draft is not exercised.

column3: A decoder treats the delta as complete at the trailer opcode; bytes after it are not read as segments.
A decoder rejects a zero-length delta before attempting any read (also section 6).
A decoder rejects a delta that ends inside an integer field.
A decoder rejects a copy segment that would take the output past the declared target length.
A decoder rejects a copy segment whose offset plus count exceeds the source length.
The offset-plus-count check is made with arithmetic that cannot overflow, so large offsets or counts cannot wrap past it.
A decoder rejects a literal segment that would take the output past the declared target length.
A decoder rejects a literal segment whose count exceeds the bytes remaining in the delta.
A decoder rejects a delta whose output length at the trailer differs from the declared target length.
A decoder rejects a segment whose opcode byte is not @, : or ;.
A decoder rejects a delta that ends without a ; trailer.
A decoder that accepts an empty, leading-zero or 2^32-or-larger integer still applies every structural and bounds check to the value it uses.
A decoder does not require, or reject a delta for, a particular segmentation or copy strategy.
A target-size query returns the header integer after reading only it and the following 0x0a; it needs no later bytes and does not validate them.
A target-size query fails on an empty buffer.
A target-size query fails when the header integer is not immediately followed by 0x0a.
The caller supplies the complete source before invoking the decoder; a delta whose source is not held is not applied.
A parser never reads past the end of the delta buffer it was given; integer accumulation stops at that boundary.
A failed delta application is never reported as success.
A caller discards the output buffer when application fails.
Bytes 0x80 through 0xFF in integer position terminate the integer; they are never decoded as digits (no high-bit masking).
A decoder treats the header's declared target length as untrusted: it does not allocate in proportion to it before the delta supplies that much output (SHOULD).
